summary: Modern databases and data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML capabilities directly where data lives, eliminating the need to move data to separate ML systems. Capabilities span in-database model training and inference (BigQuery ML, Redshift ML, Aurora ML), managed LLM functions for tasks like summarization and embedding generation (Snowflake Cortex, pgai), and native or extension-based vector search for semantic retrieval and RAG. With vector database adoption growing an estimated 377% year over year and an expected 75% of enterprise AI applications depending on vector search by 2026, general-purpose databases adding native vector capabilities are narrowing the use cases for purpose-built vector stores.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Cortex AI is Snowflake's fully managed AI layer offering serverless LLM functions (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER), embedding generation, and Cortex Search/Analyst. It runs directly on governed Snowflake data via SQL or Python, and extends to Snowflake Postgres so Postgres workloads can call Cortex AI functions.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake provides a built-in VECTOR data type plus VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY / VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE functions and Cortex Search for managed hybrid semantic search — no external extension required.
databases.llm_integration: Native, first-party. Cortex hosts foundation models (Anthropic Claude, Mistral, Meta Llama, Snowflake Arctic, and others) accessible through SQL/Python functions without managing infrastructure.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based; Cortex AI functions are billed per token/credits consumed on top of standard Snowflake compute and storage. No separate platform license.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, matrix factorization) using standard SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI for access to Gemini and other foundation models via ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, and remote model functions for in-warehouse generative AI.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery provides the VECTOR_SEARCH function and CREATE VECTOR INDEX (IVF/TreeAH) for built-in approximate nearest neighbor similarity search on embedding columns.
databases.llm_integration: Native via Vertex AI remote models — Gemini and PaLM-family models plus embedding models invoked directly from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-per-query (on-demand bytes scanned) or capacity-based slots; generative AI and embedding calls incur additional Vertex AI model charges.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: Open-source PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds a vector data type with similarity operators and HNSW/IVFFlat indexing, while pgai (and pgvectorscale) add functions to generate embeddings and call LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, Cohere) directly from SQL, keeping embeddings and data together.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL. Vector storage and similarity search require the third-party pgvector extension; pgvectorscale and pgai add scaling and model-calling. Capability depends on the extension being installed.
databases.llm_integration: Via the pgai extension, which provides SQL functions to call external LLM and embedding APIs. Not built into vanilla Postgres.
databases.pricing_notes: PostgreSQL and the extensions are free and open source; costs are the underlying compute/hosting plus any external LLM API usage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.description: Aurora ML enables SQL-based inference by integrating Aurora (PostgreSQL- and MySQL-compatible) with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock/Comprehend. Developers call ML models for predictions, text generation, and sentiment analysis directly within SQL queries against operational data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Aurora PostgreSQL supports vector search only through the third-party pgvector extension; the core Aurora ML service itself is for model inference, not built-in vector indexing.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted models through SQL functions, enabling in-database generative AI and embeddings.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Aurora instance/storage/I/O pricing; ML inference incurs separate SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend charges for the models invoked.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.description: Redshift ML allows data analysts to create, train, and deploy ML models using the CREATE MODEL SQL command, which automatically leverages Amazon SageMaker (including Autopilot) behind the scenes. Prediction is then run in-warehouse via SQL, and it also integrates with Bedrock for generative AI functions.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not natively a dedicated vector search engine. Redshift ML focuses on training/inference; vector similarity can be approximated but Redshift lacks native built-in ANN vector indexing comparable to purpose-built vector databases.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker to invoke foundation models and generate text/embeddings from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift compute (RA3/serverless) plus storage; model training and inference incur additional SageMaker/Bedrock costs.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI provides end-to-end tooling to build, fine-tune, serve, and govern generative AI and ML models, including agent frameworks, model serving, and foundation model APIs. Databricks Vector Search is a managed, serverless vector index integrated with Unity Catalog for governed semantic search and RAG.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a first-party managed vector index that auto-syncs with Delta tables and supports hybrid (semantic + keyword) retrieval.
databases.llm_integration: Native via Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs (Llama, DBRX, Claude, and others), with fine-tuning and agent orchestration built in.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks DBUs; Vector Search and Model Serving are billed per compute/endpoint usage on the Lakehouse platform.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search adds native semantic search to MongoDB's document model, letting developers store embeddings alongside operational JSON data and run approximate nearest neighbor queries using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage. It supports hybrid search combining vector and full-text relevance for RAG applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. $vectorSearch is a built-in Atlas feature with HNSW-based ANN indexing on embedding fields; no external extension required within Atlas.
databases.llm_integration: No in-database LLM hosting; integrates with external providers (OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex, LangChain, LlamaIndex) to generate embeddings and power RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Included within Atlas cluster pricing; vector search runs on dedicated Search Nodes or shared cluster resources, billed as part of Atlas consumption.
